executive_assessment.text: Dashoguz irrigation dependence, heat and water-allocation pressures differ from Ashgabat's canal/reservoir and urban supply constraints.

Vulnerable-group participation and water-quality sensitivity require attention; women-led households and migrant families were among selected local training participants, not a representative population sample.
Independent evaluation records technical capacity gains and some water-saving finance, but also limited scaling and incomplete integration of local adaptation plans.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2024-06-27 reports: Dashoguz heat days above 30°C increase by a median 18–22 days toward mid-century, from about 140 historically.
Source dated 2024-06-27 reports: Dashoguz irrigation has limited reuse, water-intensive crops and flood irrigation; farmer-managed channels face knowledge and management constraints.
Source dated 2024-06-27 reports: The assessment links climate-related water-supply pressure and demand, compounded by inefficient irrigation, to possible conflict among Dashoguz water users.
Source dated 2024-06-27 reports: Ashgabat depends on Karakum Canal reservoirs; losses, irrigation withdrawals near Mary/Tejen and shared drinking/park supply constrain water management.
Source dated 2025-06 reports: The evaluation identifies regional water cooperation and community adaptation in Lebap/Dashoguz, while noting persistent degradation and water stress.
Source dated 2025-05-20 reports: Over forty representatives joined seminars for Gorogly and Konegummez, including women-led households and families remaining behind when migrants leave.
Source dated 2025-05-20 reports: Participants practised water conservation and collaborative pasture/irrigated-land management; reported learning is not evidence of sustained adoption.
Source dated 2025-05-20 reports: The two-year IOM project partners with the environment ministry to support gender-sensitive local adaptation in Akhal and Dashoguz.
Source dated 2024-06 reports: Women managing household water, children and people with chronic illness face differentiated risks from scarcity or reduced water quality.
Source dated 2024-06 reports: Dashoguz water supply depends on Tuyamuyun reservoirs; evaporation, sedimentation and irrigation-channel losses compound climate-related scarcity.
Source dated 2024-06 reports: Proposed measures include upstream coordination, efficient irrigation and women's participation in water decisions; effectiveness is not evaluated.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 15 of 15 evidence records and 1 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
No verified armed-conflict-to-adaptation pathway or climate-caused armed violence. Conditional water-user disputes are not an armed-conflict forecast.
Local evidence focuses on Dashoguz and Ashgabat, plus selected IOM communities in Akhal; other provinces have thinner coverage.
The policy brief derives from the same 2024 risk assessment and is not independent replication. Evaluation findings cover 2021–2024, not current implementation.
National WASH and older local-project pages were inaccessible on direct opening; indexed metadata was not used.
The assessment's speculative 'climate refugees' discussion and broad mortality claims were not extracted: no supported local incidence or migration forecast was established.
Water-user conflict is a conditional planning risk, not observed violence or a forecast of armed conflict. No reverse-FCV interruption of adaptation was verified.
Assessment evidence is selective and partly stakeholder-informed; no current nationwide local vulnerability ranking is available.

The policy brief derives from the same risk assessment, not an independent study. Evaluation contributions do not establish counterfactual impacts; training and project objectives are not demonstrated adoption.
